sections.html:
Nassau County had 106,879 residents in 2025, up 18.3 percent from the 90,352 counted in the 2020 census, across 648.68 square miles of land. The typical owned home is valued at $382,800, and 82.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage carry costs of $1,849 a month. The county counted 49,001 housing units in 2025 and 1,060 building permits that year.

Newcomers arrive often, and many ask about new construction, district fees and what their own bill will look like. Ask the property appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since that gap is what a sale erases.

sections.h2: Estimating a bill for a buyer
sections.html:
The tax collector advises buyers never to treat a seller's past or current tax amount as a forecast. A new owner does not inherit the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions.

The property appraiser can help estimate upcoming taxes, but that office cannot see non-ad valorem assessments such as community development district fees. Those fees are added to the bill separately, and the estimate has to come from the district itself. If your neighborhood sits inside a district, tell the buyer so the closing numbers include it.

Setting expectations early helps. A buyer reading your old bill may expect a lower figure than reality, and a clear note about reassessment avoids a surprise at the table.

sections.h2: Bill dates and the discount schedule
sections.html:
Payment runs on a sliding monthly discount that ends March 31. Anything left unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

  • November payment: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.

Florida's revenue department places the notice of proposed taxes in August, public budget hearings in September and October, and tax bills in November. A value challenge goes to the clerk's value adjustment board petition process within 25 days of the notice. For questions about a bill, call the tax collector's tax department at 904-491-7420.

sections.h2: What to tell a buyer about the tax bill
sections.html:
Give the buyer the parcel's real situation, not a rule of thumb. A clear explanation protects both sides before a contract is signed.

  • Say whether a homestead exemption and a capped value are on the roll today, and that neither carries over.
  • Name any community development district or other non-ad valorem assessment, and give the buyer the district's contact so the buyer can ask for the amount.
  • Explain whether taxes are escrowed. If a lender pays, partial payments are discouraged and the lender sets the timing.
  • Mention any unpaid prior year, since the lien follows the land.

A buyer who learns these things at the start is less likely to ask for a credit late in the deal. A plain written summary, with a printout from the appraiser's estimate tool, makes closing day smoother. The appraiser's estimate will leave out district fees, so ask the title company to add them.

Exemptions come from the property appraiser, who takes applications each year. About 26.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, so the senior programs see steady use.

A county or city may adopt an extra senior exemption within an income limit, and another ordinance may help long-term residents with lower-value homes. Ask the property appraiser which of these apply in Nassau County or its towns.

  • A $5,000 reduction in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember.
  • A homestead discount for veteran owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A possible full homestead exemption for total and permanent disability.

A rented unit cannot keep homestead, so a landlord selling a former residence should confirm what is on the roll.

Partial payment is allowed on a current-year bill under section 197.374. The office accepts payments from November 1 through March 31, with the postmark counting. The costs are real.

  • The account loses the early-payment discount, even if the balance is later cleared in a discount month.
  • Escrowed accounts paid by a lender should not make partial payments.
  • Accounts on an installment plan should skip partial payments.
  • Whatever is unpaid on April 1 enters the delinquent process of advertising and a certificate sale.

To set one up, contact the tax department at 904-491-7420 or taxes@nassautaxes.com. Payments can then be made in person, by mail or online.

The tax collector must hold a certificate sale on or before June 1, conducted online on the LienHub platform.

Nassau tax certificate terms
TermRule
Sale deadlineOn or before June 1 each year
BiddingDownward on interest, starting at 18 percent; lowest bidder wins
Minimum earned5 percent until accrued interest exceeds it; zero-interest bids earn zero
Lien statusEnforceable first lien on the real estate
ValiditySeven years from issuance
Tax deed applicationAfter two or more years of delinquency

To remove the lien, the owner pays the collector all delinquent tax plus interest, costs and other charges. A certificate holder cannot demand payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issuance year, and a deed application carries a $75 fee. Homestead land with a small delinquency goes to the county rather than to a bidder.

If you are behind, call the tax department before the June sale. Paying early limits the added costs, and a title company can pay the full amount from your sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Homestead rules and deed taxes in a sale
sections.html:
The standard exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value and is filed by March 1. Capped assessment growth was 2.7 percent for 2026. A buyer's value starts over after a sale.

Deed stamps follow section 201.02 at 70 cents on every $100 of price. Liability sits with all parties to the deed, and payment goes to the clerk at recording.

sections.h2: Steps before you accept an offer
sections.html:
Check the parcel record for the right owner name and mailing address. Ask the tax department whether any year is unpaid and request a written payoff. Find out whether a district assessment applies, and ask the district for its current amount. Ask the title company how the sale year's taxes will be prorated, then confirm the plan in the contract.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip lender timelines, but unpaid taxes, district fees and recorded liens are still settled from the sale proceeds before the deed is recorded. Keep your closing statement and the paid receipts together, since a later question about the sale year's bill is easier to answer with them in hand.

faqs.q: Does a new Nassau County owner get the seller's tax amount?
faqs.a: No. The buyer does not benefit from the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions, so past bills are not a safe estimate.

faqs.q: Do community development district fees show on the appraiser's estimate?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser cannot see non-ad valorem assessments, so ask the district for its amount, which is then added to the tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I lose the discount if I make a partial payment in Nassau County?
faqs.a: Yes. The account is no longer eligible for discount even if the rest is paid during a discount month. Partial payments run November 1 through March 31.

faqs.q: When does Nassau County sell tax certificates?
faqs.a: The sale is held by June 1 each year on the LienHub site. Bids start at 18 percent and fall, and the lowest rate takes the certificate.

faqs.q: How long before a tax deed can be sought on a Nassau County parcel?
faqs.a: The certificate holder may apply once two or more years of delinquency have run. Until then, the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest, costs and charges.
